record.kind: OnSpawnEffect (shared instance) gated on rain weather
record.summary: PassiveEffects[Passive.AQUA_VEIL] holds one OnSpawnEffect. When the unit's entity is spawned for a fight (after synergy and item effects) it checks entity.simulation.weather: only if the weather is RAIN does it call status.triggerRuneProtect(60000, entity, entity). triggerRuneProtect sets runeProtect = true, zeroes the cooldowns of the negative statuses the unit already has, and sets runeProtectCooldown to 60000 ms unless a longer value is already there. The cooldown counts down in the status update (runeProtect becomes false when it runs out), so the protection lasts 60000 ms of simulated time. In any other weather the effect does nothing. Rune Protect blocks new applications of the status triggers that check !runeProtect; it is not the Protect status and blocks neither damage nor ordinary healing (core-mechanics §J: status.protect versus status.runeProtect).
triggers: OnSpawnEffect applied in Simulation.addPokemon when the entity is created (fight start or later spawn)
OnSpawnEffect of the rebuilt clone in PokemonEntity.resurrect (see unresolved)

effects.declaredRaw: Rune Protect for 60000 ms (duration requested), only when the simulation's weather is RAIN
effects.scaling: none: no AP, crit or star scaling; the duration is a fixed constant. triggerRuneProtect does not apply the status-duration reductions that other triggers use; it only keeps the larger of the new timer and the existing runeProtectCooldown.
effects.resolution: requested 60000 ms; applied = 60000 ms unless a longer runeProtectCooldown already exists (a fresh entity starts at 0); the count-down runs in the status update. The negative-status cooldowns already on the entity are zeroed at the same time (nothing is applied to a fresh entity at spawn, so this matters only for later spawns).

effects.declaredRaw: runeProtect = true makes status triggers that check !runeProtect do nothing
effects.resolution: only status applications are refused where the code checks the flag; damage, healing and PP gain are unaffected by Rune Protect alone (they depend on status.protect, see core-mechanics §J).
